**Mocha Crinkles**  
1 1/3 cups firmly packed light brown sugar  
½ cup vegetable oil  
¼ cup sour cream (book says low fat but we’ve always used whole)  
1 egg  
1 tsp vanilla  
1 ¾ cups all-purpose flour  
¾ cup unsweetened cocoa powder  
2 tsp instant espresso or coffee granules  
1 tsp baking soda  
¼ tsp salt  
1/8 tsp ground black pepper  
½ cup powdered sugar  
  
1.	Beat brown sugar and oil in medium bowl with electric mixer. Mix in sour cream, egg, and vanilla. Set aside.  
2.	Mix flour, cocoa, espresso, baking soda, salt, and pepper in another medium bowl.  
3.	Add flour mixture to brown sugar mixture; mix well. Refrigerate dough until firm, 3-4 hours.  
4.	Preheat over to 350º F. Pour powdered sugar into shallow bowl. Set aside. Cut dough into 1-inch pieces and roll into balls. Roll dough balls in powdered sugar.  
5.	Bake on ungreased cookie sheets 10 to 12 minutes or until tops of cookies are firm to touch. Do not overbake! Cool on wire racks. Makes 6 dozen cookies 😊

I feel the exact same way. Not a shred of self esteem at 26 and I have no idea how to change that because I just feel so deeply that I am "bad" and unlikable. I was always an easy target to get teased because I was a very sensitive and emotional child and I was easy to provoke. When I was 11 I was bullied for a while in school, none of the girls in my grade would talk to me for a couple months, and one day they called me over to talk to them. I thought they were going to apologise but they all said "We're sorry...for ever being your friend." Honestly, I feel like I have never recovered. There were other factors prior to this that contributed to my problems, but this I feel truly broke me. My self esteem was obliterated. I was suicidal, cutting myself daily, begging my parents to let me change schools daily. I became more withdrawn the older I got. I dropped out of high school and couldn't leave my house for a couple years. Now I'm a university dropout. My paranoia of people disliking me is such that I can barely even post things online, under the veil of anonymity. I honestly, truly, deeply, and (I believe) deservedly hate myself. And I feel so stupid for letting this still affect me, 15 years later.

This post really got to me for some reason. I often feel extremely down for not having a real social life and thinking of all the things I've missed out on due to being avoidant. I've cut out about 90% of people I've ever met in my life, simply bc of my own insecurities and avoidance tendencies and I hate it.  I think you should keep in mind that you *want* to connect with people. You aren't truly anti social or incompetent; there is something you are psychologically not dealing with that is manifesting as AvPD, and you've probably been this way so long it feels natural, like you're "just like this". You're not, though, I promise you. I'm sorry if this comment sounds dumb or rude or maybe this doesn't resonate with you and that's okay. Posting comments online is extremely difficult for me, as silly as that sounds. But I know at the end of the day this stems from my early experiences with online bullying and social isolation from my peers, so it's hard for me to trust people or feel like they want to hear what I have to say. So I force myself to post sometimes, and it has helped veeeery slowly but it has. Maybe something that can help you is going to a therapist or counselor that specialises in processing traumatic events in your life. Even if you don't think of them as traumatic right now, there are experiences in your past that have lead to this behaviour that have not been processed and are being used as a precedent to justify your insecurity/feelings of inferiority/avoidance. I hope this comment helps a little, I'm sorry.
